title: Re-derive submission validity on the server instead of trusting the client boolean
description:
web_intake_service.py:796-797 is the whole server-side validity gate: if completion.get('valid') is not True: raise. The browser computes that boolean; the server never re-derives it. With the Python evaluator from digitva-cal.1 in place, the server can evaluate relevant and constraint itself over the submitted answers and stop trusting the client.

Threat model, stated: interviewers are authenticated staff, not the public, so this is not an open-internet hole. It is still a gate that does nothing, and a crafted request can store a date of death before the date of birth or an ABHA number failing its regex.
design:
DECIDED by the owner 2026-09-20, two parts.

PART 1 -- log and accept, do not reject. The first release evaluates relevant and constraint server-side but does NOT refuse a submission that only the server considers invalid. It records the disagreement and stores the answers. Reason: if the server starts rejecting what the client accepted, an interviewer in the field is stuck with no recourse and no way to complete a death record. Once the real mismatch volume is known from live data, a later release can flip to refusing -- that flip is a separate decision, not part of this bead.

The client's own boolean keeps its existing power in one direction only: if the client says invalid, the submission is still refused, exactly as today. The server never accepts that boolean as PROOF of validity.

PART 2 -- record each mismatch as a validation_err on the response itself, not only in a log line. A log is not queryable, rotates away, and nobody reads it; the point is to learn how often the two engines disagree and on which questions, which means the data has to live with the submission. Additive, reversible migration.

Each entry carries: the question name, which rule disagreed (relevant or constraint), and that the client claimed valid. It carries NO answer values -- these records are PII and a validation error must not become a side channel that copies answers into a new column, an export or a log. Also return the entries in the HTTP response to the submitting client, which costs nothing and makes a field problem debuggable.

Open sub-question for whoever implements: whether validation_err belongs on va_submissions or on va_submission_payload_versions. Prefer the payload version if a resubmission should be able to disagree differently from its predecessor -- that is the more useful history. State the choice and why.
acceptance_criteria: A submission whose answers violate a constraint is STORED, not refused, when the payload claims valid=true, and carries a validation_err entry naming the question and the rule. A submission the client marks invalid is still refused. Valid submissions carry no entries and are unaffected -- prove that against the existing web-intake tests. No answer values in the stored entries, the HTTP response, or any log line. Migration is additive and reversible.
notes:
Blocked on digitva-cal.1 (the Python evaluator). Sequencing note: a later release may flip from accept-and-record to refuse; the data this bead collects is what should inform that, so do not build the refusal path now. Settled 2026-09-20: validation_err lives on va_submission_payload_versions, not va_submissions. That table is genuinely per-version, with a version_status lifecycle (active / pending_upstream / superseded / rejected) and a unique-active index per va_sid, so a resubmission creates a new version and its disagreement record belongs with the answers it describes rather than being overwritten on the parent row. Storing it on va_submissions would lose the history that makes the accept-and-record release worth doing.

When adding the column, do not repeat the doubled-constraint-name bug catalogued in the CHECK-constraint bead: pass only the discriminator to any new constraint, never the ck_<table>_ prefixed form.

---

title: Port the XLSForm expression evaluator to Python, with a conformance corpus
description:
Decided by the owner 2026-09-20: Python must parse the instrument JSON and assess response validity itself, so the browser stops being the single enforcement point (digitva-cal). This is step one -- the evaluator alone, no behaviour change to intake yet.

Scope is bounded and known. vendor/who-va-2022/src/engine/expression.ts is 402 lines. The instrument carries 445 expressions, 277 unique, across three fields: relevant (318), constraint (89), calculation (38). The complete function set used is: selected, if, not, and, or, regex, today, date, int, string-length, count-selected. Nothing else appears.
design:
THE CENTRAL RISK is two evaluators that drift, which is exactly what the expression-tokenizer bug in 78757d4 showed can happen invisibly. The port is only acceptable if divergence fails a test.

So the deliverable is two things, and the corpus matters more than the port:
1. A conformance corpus GENERATED FROM THE TYPESCRIPT ENGINE: every unique expression in the instrument, evaluated against a set of answer fixtures, with its result recorded as golden output in a committed JSON file. A tooling script under tooling/who-va-2022/ produces it, deterministically, the way build-layer-reference.mjs does.
2. A Python evaluator asserted against that corpus, case by case. A test that reads the corpus and requires identical results for every case, including error cases.

KNOWN DIVERGENCE TRAPS, found by inspection 2026-09-20 -- each needs a corpus case:
* Python re matches Unicode digits with \\d by default; JavaScript RegExp does not. The instrument contains regex(.,'^(?!0{1,3}$)\\d{1,3}$') on sa13-sa19, so a Devanagari or Bengali digit would pass server-side and fail client-side. Use re.ASCII or explicit ASCII classes and pin it with a case.
* XPath 1.0 string literals have no escape mechanism; a backslash is an ordinary character (established in 78757d4). The doubled-quote convention is the only escape.
* today() and date arithmetic: timezone handling must match, and the app is timezone-aware throughout.
* Empty and missing answers: isEmpty/asBoolean/asNumber/equal in expression.ts have specific coercion semantics. Port them literally rather than reaching for Python truthiness.
* Numeric comparison of ISO date strings via dateNumber.

No change to web_intake_service or session behaviour in this work package. Evaluator plus corpus plus tests only.
acceptance_criteria: A committed corpus covering all 277 unique instrument expressions with golden results from the TypeScript engine. A Python evaluator that reproduces every one. Regenerating the corpus on an unmodified tree reproduces it byte for byte. Reverting any single semantic fix in the Python evaluator fails at least one corpus case -- demonstrate that, do not assert it.
close_reason: Landed in e77c293. Python evaluator plus a conformance corpus of 347 unique expressions and 1,903 cases generated from the TypeScript engine, pinned byte for byte and asserted case by case. Distribution confirms it is not vacuous (334 true, 1,351 false, 60 NaN, 59 strings). The deliberate-regression requirement was met by demonstration, reproduced independently in the main session: removing the six re.ASCII guards reports '1 of 1903 corpus cases diverged'; restoring them passes. Surfaced a second Unicode-digit bug in the tokenizer's own numeric-literal detection. Two unportable JS behaviours recorded rather than hidden. digitva-cal.2 (server-side validity, accept-and-record) is now unblocked.

title: Machine-translated strings must not be served until a human reviews them
description:
Migration b6d2f4a9c1e7 seeded 214 machine-translated strings with source='imported' -- the same value workbook-sourced strings carry. Nothing in the database distinguishes 'came from a deployed ODK form' from 'Claude wrote it', and approval is per-locale, so approving a locale blesses both at once. On the owner's dev database all thirteen locales are approved and active, which means unreviewed machine translations are being served to web forms right now.

Owner's intent, stated 2026-09-20: only the workbook-imported translations are approved; the machine-translated ones need review. They must remain visible and editable in the panel -- deletion is explicitly not wanted, because it removes the very content someone has to review.
design:
Third source value SOURCE_MACHINE = 'machine' (source is String(16), no CHECK constraint, so no widening needed).

1. Migration relabels the 214 seeded rows imported -> machine, matching on the exact literals from b6d2f4a9c1e7 so a row an administrator has already corrected or that no longer matches is left alone. Reversible.
2. export_translations excludes source='machine', so the served payload omits them and the client falls back to English per string -- the same mechanism an untranslated string already uses. This is the whole fix: the strings exist, are listed, are editable, and are not served.
3. The panel marks machine rows distinctly and offers an accept-as-is action that promotes machine -> edited without retyping. update_string already sets edited, so an admin who edits the text is already covered; the gap is only accepting a good machine string unchanged.
4. A workbook re-import must overwrite a machine row: workbook beats machine, while edited still beats both. Today the importer keeps edited and overwrites imported; machine must join the overwritable side.
5. Per-extension coverage should not count machine rows as translated, or the panel will report a locale as complete on strings that are not being served.
acceptance_criteria: A locale with machine rows serves English for exactly those items and its own workbook translations for the rest. The panel lists machine rows, marks them, and can promote one to edited. A workbook re-import overwrites a machine row and never an edited one. Coverage does not count machine rows. Tests pin each of these.
close_reason: Machine-translated strings are now a distinct source='machine', relabelled by migration c1a4b6e8d3f2, excluded from export_translations and from coverage, visible and acceptable in the panel via POST .../strings/accept. Precedence edited > imported > machine holds without importer changes (only SOURCE_EDITED was ever special-cased). Constraint renamed to ck_mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved by d2b5c7f9e4a3 and the model now passes only the discriminator. Review found one real gap, fixed before commit: export_xliff labelled machine rows state='translated', so a CAT tool showed unreviewed drafts as finished; they now export as initial with subState digitva:machine, and an unmapped source understates rather than claiming translated.

title: Web form locale codes: column default 'en' is not a seeded mas_languages code
description: va_project_master.web_intake_default_locale defaults to 'en' (model and migration f2a9c4d7e1b3) but flask seed run creates mas_languages codes 'english', 'hindi', ... (app/commands/seed.py). Consequences on every seeded deployment: (1) the form-options resolver in app/routes/api/organization.py logs 'en is not an active language' and falls back to the first active code, so on dev every project's web form opens with locale='assamese'; (2) the projects admin panel now shows 'en (inactive)' and blocks Save until an admin picks an active code. Deeper question: the WHO VA web component's locale attribute expects instrument locale codes ('English (en)' in the bundle), not mas_languages codes, which exist for narration-language alias mapping. Decide: either seed short locale codes / add a locale_code column on mas_languages that the resolver serves, or map at the endpoint. Domain decision, not for an agent to take.

title: Rebuild the translation editor as a per-question workspace
description:
Owner's design, 2026-09-21. The current editor is a flat, alphabetical list of strings with an inline textarea per row. Replace it with a list ordered the way the questionnaire is ordered, where each row is a QUESTION and editing opens a modal carrying that question's whole package: label, hint, constraint message, and the options of any choice list it uses. Reviewing a translation then means reviewing a complete unit rather than a string torn out of context -- which is exactly how the Odia and Hindi defects escaped notice.

LIST VIEW: read-only. Columns, in this order: question code, English label, the locale's label. Ordered by the question's position in the form, not alphabetically. Paginate 50 questions per page (note: pagination unit changes from strings to questions).

MODAL: opens for one question and holds every translatable item for it -- label, hint, constraint message, and each option of its choice list. Save writes them together.

CHOICE LISTS ARE SHARED: a list belongs to many questions (YES_NO_DK_REF backs 224). Editing an option updates it for every question that uses that list -- which is already how storage works, keyed by list_name/value. The modal must SAY so, with the count, or an editor will believe they are making a local change.

RICH TEXT: the source carries ODK markup -- 337 questions have <span style="color:blue"> in guidance, 51 hints and 6 labels carry HTML. The list and modal must RENDER it, not display raw tags, and the modal needs a toolbar for bold, italic and coloured span.
design:
THREE DEPENDENCIES, none of them optional.

1. CONSTRAINT MESSAGES DO NOT EXIST AS TRANSLATIONS. 89 of 449 questions carry one; the field is not in _TRANSLATABLE_FIELDS, zero rows are stored, and NO deployed workbook has a constraint_message:: column in any language -- so there is nothing to import. Putting them in the modal means adding the field to the translatable set AND authoring the target text, the way the DigitVA layer strings were authored. Until then the modal can show the English read-only, but the owner should decide which.

2. ORDERING AND GROUPING NEED THE INSTRUMENT. map_instrument_translations stores item_kind/item_key/field with no notion of question order or which list a question uses. list_strings returns flat rows. The panel must join against the generated instrument JSON (which has order, listName and choices) to sort by form position and to group options under their questions. That is the real work in this issue.

3. THE RENDERER ALREADY EXISTS -- REUSE IT. vendor/who-va-2022/src/ui/rich-text.ts parses exactly this markup into styled spans and deliberately avoids innerHTML so hostile content degrades to visible text. It is NOT currently exported from the built bundle. Re-export parseRichText from tooling/who-va-2022/entry.mjs rather than writing a second parser for the admin page: two renderers would drift, and the admin editor showing something different from the form is the failure this whole issue exists to prevent. The toolbar must emit the same subset that parser accepts, or an editor will produce markup the form renders as literal text.

Guidance is a fourth, smaller gap: the service lists it as translatable and 338 questions have it, but zero rows exist because the workbooks ship guidance_hint::English only.
acceptance_criteria: List ordered by form position, 50 questions per page, columns question code / English / locale text, read-only, markup rendered. Modal edits a question's label, hint and choice options together and states how many questions share each list. Rich-text toolbar emits only what parseRichText accepts. Constraint messages either editable or explicitly shown read-only per the owner's decision.
notes:
CLARIFIED 2026-09-21 (owner): the Google Translate button is PER TEXT, not per question. Each individual text in the modal -- the question label, the hint, each choice option, the read-only guidance and constraint message -- carries its own small button beside it, and clicking it opens Google Translate with THAT ONE FIELD's English only. Nothing is concatenated: no 'translate the whole question', no bundling label with hint. The editor is working on one field at a time and wants that field's text.

This also mostly dissolves the URL-length worry recorded earlier: a single label or choice option is short. Only a long guidance block can approach a problematic URL, and guidance is read-only anyway, so if any field needs truncation or omission it is that one.
close_reason: Delivered in 5618e07. Own page at /admin/instrument-translations/<instrument>/<locale> with page and search in the URL; one row per question in form order (code, English, locale text) covering all 449 WHO questions plus 80 DigitVA layer questions and 10 orphan choice lists, 536 rows for hi; modal edits label, hint and choice options, shows constraint message and guidance read-only badged untranslated, warns how many questions a shared list changes, and offers Save, Save and next, Undo and Close with dirty tracking; per-field Google Translate links, hidden for Khasi; markup rendered through the form's own parseRichText, re-exported from the bundle rather than reimplemented. Full suite 1729 passed; verified in a browser rather than on report. The authoring of untranslated constraint messages and guidance was detached to its own issue: it is independent work, not unfinished work here.

title: Kannada select_531 stores English 'Don't know' as a translation
description: KA01_DS_WHOVA2022.xlsx, label::Kannada (kn), list select_531, row 308 (value 'dk'), used by Id10484. The cell is literally "Don't know\n" -- English plus a trailing empty line, no Kannada at all, while every sibling in the list has real Kannada. split_packed has no second non-empty line to treat as the translation, so DigitVA stores and serves the ENGLISH string as though it were Kannada, and counts it toward coverage. This is the general hazard worth checking for elsewhere: a single-line packed cell can launder English into the translation table. Kannada is already demoted for other reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Either split_packed refuses a single-line cell rather than storing English as a translation, or the case is documented as accepted with the reasoning; this row corrected.

title: Show English alongside the translation in the web form
description: Proposed by the owner 2026-09-20, prompted by digitva-fb5. The deployed ODK forms pack English and the translation into one cell, so an interviewer there sees BOTH lines. That is why OD01's Odia defect (Id10192 carrying Id10191's wording) is survivable in ODK: the correct English sits directly above the wrong translation. DigitVA's web form serves only the translated half, so the same defect has nothing beside it to catch it -- we are strictly less safe than the form we replace. Showing both would restore that cross-check, and would also change what demoting a locale costs: instead of falling back to English entirely, a locale under review could be shown WITH English alongside, staying useful where it is right and visibly wrong where it is not. Client-side change in app/static/js/intake/ and the web component; applyTranslations already has both strings in hand (the bundle carries English, the payload carries the locale), so no API or schema change is implied.
design: Owner decided 2026-09-21: (1) toggle, default ON; (2) labels, choices AND hints; (3) in_review locales become selectable in the web form WITH English alongside -- main session adds: toggle is locked on for in_review locales, so English can never be hidden under an unreviewed translation. Approved locales keep the toggle.
acceptance_criteria: Decided and recorded in docs/policy/va-web-form-options.md before implementation; the display works for question text at minimum; no change to what is stored in a submission.
close_reason: English alongside translation: toggle default on, labels/hints/choices; in_review locales served with English forced on; draft never served. Policy recorded, full suite 1,736 passed, verified in browser.

title: Stand up a working web-intake demo project end to end
description: Demo (ZZD001) is the only project with web_intake_mode set, but the project is inactive and has no active web form, so readiness reports NOT READY on two of nine checks. Reactivate it, materialize the per-site web forms through ensure_web_forms_for_project (not raw SQL, which skips the side effect), confirm an interviewer grant resolves, then drive the browser form end to end and submit one record. This is the first time browser capture is exercised by a human path rather than tests: all 9,353 existing payload versions came from ODK sync and the drafts table is empty.
acceptance_criteria: flask web-intake readiness ZZD001 reports READY; a named interviewer can open /intake/, fill and submit; the submission lands with a payload version whose created_by_role is not vasystem; drafts and validation_err behave as documented.
close_reason: Demo (ZZD001) now reports READY on all nine checks (one WARN: no org tree, which is documented as harmless). Project reactivated and the per-site web form ZZD001Z00102 materialized through ensure_web_forms_for_project, not raw SQL, so the side effect the admin route relies on actually ran. Verified in a browser: /intake/ lists drafts, the questionnaire renders from today's V2.0 English-only instrument (the sex choices read 'Intersex/Ambiguous', V2.0's wording), answers validate and persist, the draft autosaves, and switching to Hindi translates labels, hints, choices and section names with answers intact -- which proves the English-only bundle plus translation engine works end to end. Not done: a complete 450-question submission, which is a human task; surfaced digitva-fb5 on the way.

title: Adopt WHO V2.0 as the curated reference form, English only, with two deviations
description: Rebuild vendor/who-va-2022/src/generated/who-va-2022.instrument.json from 2022whova_xls_form_for_odk_multilingual.xlsx (V2.0, 2026081401) via app/services/xlsform_instrument_builder.py. Decisions recorded in docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md: instrument carries English only (all other locales come from map_instrument_translations); Id10304_a keeps V1.1 relevance as a DEVIATION (WHO defect, SwissTPH/WHO-VA#94); Id10230 keeps agegroup C_A as a DEVIATION (wider beats narrower). Accept Id10191 agegroup N->C_A and the 15 English label/hint changes. Builder needs a locale-selection parameter so a multilingual workbook can emit English only. Then regenerate the expression conformance corpus, the server instrument and the browser bundle, and re-audit DEVIATIONS.
design: The builder already reproduces V1.1 byte-for-byte outside DEVIATIONS, so this is a rebuild and reconciliation, not the editorial work the earlier handoff described. Inline locales were measured as stale and shadowed before being dropped: engine 260 French choice labels vs inline 144, 53 of the 142 shared differing, engine holding the newer text.
acceptance_criteria: test_xlsform_instrument_builder.py passes with DEVIATIONS covering exactly Id10304_a.relevant and Id10230.ageGroup beyond the existing eleven; instrument carries no locale but en; corpus and bundle regenerated; full suite green.
close_reason: Delivered in db18a0f. Instrument rebuilt from V2.0 English-only via a new locales parameter on build_instrument_from_xlsform (default unchanged). Id10304_a keeps V1.1 relevance and Id10230 keeps agegroup C_A, both as DEVIATIONS and both documented in vendor/who-va-2022/README.md. Corpus and layer reference regenerate byte-identical; server instrument and browser bundle rebuilt. Full suite 1714 passed PYTEST_EXIT=0, vendored JS 28 passed, bundle verified to carry the two deviations, V2.0 English text and no locale key.

title: Record the WHO V2.0 Id10304_a unreachable-relevance defect and confirm deployed forms are unaffected
description: WHO's multilingual V2.0 release (version 2026081401) changes Id10304_a's relevant from selected(${Id10304},'yes') to selected(${Id10334},'yes') and selected(${Id10305},'yes'). The two conjuncts are mutually exclusive because Id10334's own relevance contains not(selected(${Id10305},'yes')), so the question becomes unreachable. Retain the analysis, the comparison diagram and the reproduction in docs/kb/WHO_VA_2022_Docs/, and record that all ten deployed site workbooks carry the V1.1 rule and are unaffected. Blocks adopting V2.0 verbatim under digitva-13x.
acceptance_criteria: Finding documented with the enumeration reproducible; diagram retained in repo; deployed-form verdict recorded; README inventory links it; digitva-13x references it.
notes: WHO replied 2026-09-21 on #95 only: agegroup is an internal marker, filters no question, no effect on the flow -- confirming our own finding that nothing in DigitVA branches on ageGroup. The reply does NOT address #94 (Id10304_a unreachable relevance), which is the defect that actually removes a question from interviews. Keep this bead open until #94 is answered.

title: Dev database's va_user_access_grants CHECK omits collaborator_pii
description:
Found 2026-09-20 while verifying that renaming CHECK constraints preserved their logic -- the rename did not cause this, it merely exposed it.

Comparing pg_get_constraintdef between the dev database and a database built from the migration chain alone:

  dev:   role = ANY (ARRAY['collaborator', 'coder', 'coding_tester', 'reviewer', 'data_manager', 'interviewer'])
  fresh: role = ANY (ARRAY['collaborator', 'collaborator_pii', 'coder', 'coding_tester', 'reviewer', 'data_manager', 'interviewer'])

So on dev, inserting a va_user_access_grants row with role='collaborator_pii' is refused by the database, while a fresh deployment accepts it. The scope_shape and role_scope constraints are the ones guarding authorization shape, so this is an authorization-relevant divergence, not cosmetic.

The test suite cannot see it: tests build their schema with db.create_all() from the models, never from the migration chain, and tests/migrations/test_schema_drift.py compares a fresh migration-built database against the models -- neither ever inspects the long-lived dev database. So dev can drift from both without any test noticing.
design:
First establish which is correct: does the model declare collaborator_pii, and did a migration add it that dev never received, or was it removed from dev by hand? git log -S collaborator_pii over the migrations and the model will say.

If a migration adds it and dev simply missed it, the fix is operational -- replay the migration on dev -- not a code change. If no migration adds it, then a fresh install and the models are ahead of every migration, which is a real chain gap and needs one.

Related but distinct from digitva-2g7 (dev and a fresh clone differing on the old WHO_2022_VA bucket scheme). The two together suggest the dev database has accumulated more than one divergence from its own migration history, which is worth a single sweep comparing dev against a fresh replay across all constraints, defaults and enums rather than finding them one at a time.
acceptance_criteria: The correct definition is established from the migration history, dev matches it, and it is recorded whether this was operational drift or a missing migration. If a sweep is done, its findings are filed.
notes:
TRACED 2026-09-20: this is operational drift on the dev database, not a missing migration. Two committed migrations carry the role -- f1c6a9d3e7b5_add_collaborator_pii_role.py (added in c04662c) and a40c38e73af4_add_org_unit_coding_gate.py (3a17d8c) -- and the dev database is long past both, since f1c6a9d3e7b5 is the root of the chain recorded in handoff.md. A database built from the chain alone has the role; dev does not. So dev's constraint was recreated or altered outside the chain at some point.

Fix is therefore operational for dev: bring that one constraint into line with what the migrations produce. No application change. Worth doing the wider dev-versus-fresh sweep described in the design field at the same time, because two independent divergences (this and digitva-2g7) is evidence of a pattern rather than an accident.
close_reason: Closed

title: Strip irrelevant answers at final submit, keep them in the draft
description:
Decided by the owner 2026-09-20: clear non-relevant responses at final submit; drafts retain everything so an answer reverted by a mis-tap can be recovered.

Today relevance is presentational: vendor/who-va-2022/src/engine/session.ts never clears an answer that becomes irrelevant, so an interviewer can photograph md_im1-md_im4, set md_available to no, and submit a record that says no medical records exist while carrying four photographs of them.
design:
Filter at payload build on final submit only. The draft is untouched, which is the whole point of the owner's decision: toggling a gate back restores the answers.

This depends on digitva-cal.1: deciding which answers are irrelevant means evaluating relevant server-side, and no Python evaluator exists until that lands.

Cascade matters. Hiding md_available hides md_count which hides md_im1-30, so the filter must resolve relevance transitively over the submitted answers rather than one level. Removing an answer can itself change nothing else's relevance here (relevance reads answers, and a removed answer is empty) -- verify that rather than assuming it, and if a fixed point is needed, iterate to one.

Attachments: an image answer stripped from the payload may already have an uploaded file behind it. Decide and document what happens to that file -- orphaning it is the failure attachments phase 2 turns into real wasted storage. Do not silently leave it.
acceptance_criteria: A submission where a gate was answered no after images were captured stores no image answers, and the draft still holds them. Cascaded relevance is resolved transitively, pinned by a test over md_available/md_count/md_im*. What happens to an already-uploaded attachment behind a stripped answer is implemented and documented, not left implicit.
notes: Implemented via the same app/services/web_form_relevance_service.py: strip_irrelevant_answers resolves md_available->md_count->md_im* to a fixed point (2 passes needed, not 1 -- proven by test). Requires vendor/who-va-2022/src/generated/who-va-2022.server-instrument.json, generated by new tooling/who-va-2022/build-server-instrument.mjs (npm run build:server-instrument). Attachment refs behind stripped answers: today nothing is orphaned server-side since who-va-attachment: values are client-local blob ids uploaded in a not-yet-built phase 2; documented in build_web_payload's docstring and docs/policy/va-web-form-options.md. Not closed per instructions.
close_reason: Closed

title: Report coverage against all translatable strings, not base question labels only
description:
Coverage is computed against reference_label_keys() -- 476 base question labels -- so every locale reports 100.0% while roughly a third of its translatable text is untranslated. Measured on dev 2026-09-20.

The reference holds 1,435 translatable items: 556 question labels, 340 guidance hints, 215 hints, 324 choice labels. Against that denominator every locale sits at 66-68%. Against all question labels including the DigitVA layers (556) they sit at 86-87%. Against the base-only 476 they report 100%.

Two defects, not one. The measure is too narrow: hints, guidance hints and choice labels are translatable, are served, and are invisible to the number. And the denominator is stale: base-only stopped being correct for labels the moment layer questions became translatable (digitva-thr), which is why Khasi reads 100% holding exactly 476 of 556 labels -- every base label, no layer labels.

Owner's instruction 2026-09-20: measure total translatable strings against translated strings.
design:
Headline coverage becomes translated / all translatable reference items, with the label figure kept as a breakdown rather than deleted -- both are useful, only one should be the headline. Per-extension coverage likewise counts every item kind, not just labels; extension_label_keys is label-only today and needs an all-items sibling.

Must exclude source='machine' rows once digitva-4kj lands, or the honest denominator gets a dishonest numerator.

Coverage still decides nothing (2026-09-19 decision stands): this changes what the number says, never what it gates.

Expect a documentation sweep, not just a code change: every claim that a locale is at 100 percent becomes false, including docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md, docs/current-state/admin-and-setup.md, cli-reference.md and handoff.md. The 'all thirteen documented languages reach 100 percent coverage on the survey labels' line in handoff.md is true only of the narrow measure and must say which one it means.
acceptance_criteria: locale_status and the panel report translated/total over all translatable items, with the label-only figure shown as a breakdown. Per-extension coverage counts all item kinds. machine rows count toward neither. A test pins the denominator at the reference's full item count so a future change to the reference cannot silently narrow it again. Docs no longer claim 100 percent without naming the measure.
notes:
Blocked on digitva-4kj: both change coverage computation in app/services/instrument_translation_service.py and the same panel and docs, so they must not run concurrently.

DOC SCOPE, measured 2026-09-20 rather than assumed -- it is small. Three places mention 100 percent and all three already name their measure: docs/current-state/admin-and-setup.md:313 ('base coverage (WHO survey labels, informational)'), handoff.md:220 ('100 percent on the base instrument'), handoff.md:340 ('100 percent coverage on the survey labels'). None is false; each is narrow. So this is not a sweep of wrong claims -- it is a change to which number is the headline, plus making these three say so explicitly. An earlier note on this bead implied a larger documentation problem; that was wrong.

VERIFIED PREMISE for the fallback these numbers describe: export_translations (app/services/instrument_translation_service.py, the questions/choices loop) builds its dicts only from rows that exist, so an untranslated item is ABSENT from the served payload rather than an empty string. Per-string English fallback is real, confirmed by reading the code 2026-09-20, not inferred from a report.
close_reason: Coverage headline is now translated/all translatable reference items (1,435: 556 question labels, 340 guidance hints, 215 hints, 324 choice labels), with question-label coverage kept as a breakdown. reference_label_keys broadened from base-only 476 to 556 -- the stale-denominator half of the bug, which is why every locale read 100 percent while a third of its text was untranslated. Per-extension coverage counts all item kinds with label sub-figures. machine rows count toward neither. Denominator pinned by a test against the real committed reference, so re-narrowing fails. Thirteen locales now read 66.0-66.3 percent headline, 85.6 percent labels, matching an independent measurement. Review found three stale narrow-vs-wide claims in untouched code and docs (a panel tooltip calling item counts labels, and two admin-and-setup passages describing the old semantics); all three fixed before commit.

title: Decide whether a bulk re-import knocks an approved locale back to in_review
description:
The approval gate holds for a NEW locale but not for an existing one. An admin can re-import any workbook (the documented-source name gate was removed 2026-09-20) or POST an XLIFF hand-back into a live, approved, active locale: version bumps, every string can change, and the locale stays approved and keeps being served. Nobody re-reviews the new content.

digitva-j23's premise was 'incomplete, in-process or unverified translations must not be offered to users'. That is satisfied for a locale nobody has approved yet, and defeated for one that was approved before its content was rewritten. Found by audit 2026-09-20; import_translations, update_string and import_xliff contain no reference to lifecycle_state, which was implemented as specified and is correct as far as it goes.
design:
DECIDED by the owner 2026-09-20: yes, a bulk re-import knocks an approved locale back to in_review -- but only after warning, never silently.

Rule: when import_translations or import_xliff writes to a locale whose lifecycle_state is 'approved', the locale returns to in_review, approved_by_user_id and approved_at are cleared, and is_active is set false (the CHECK constraint requires it). The import still proceeds. update_string is explicitly NOT affected: an administrator editing one string IS the reviewer, and the new per-string Accept action is the same case.

'After warning' means the caller must acknowledge before anything is written, and each surface warns in its own idiom:
* CLI: refuse and explain unless an explicit flag is passed; the message must name the locale, that it is approved and active, and that proceeding takes it off the forms until re-approved.
* Admin panel: a confirmation step stating the same consequence before the request is sent.
* API/route: an explicit acknowledgement field, so a scripted caller cannot demote a live locale by accident. Absent it, refuse with a message naming what would happen.

The import report names the demotion so it appears in output and logs.
acceptance_criteria: Importing into an approved locale without acknowledgement is refused, with a message naming the locale and the consequence. With acknowledgement the import proceeds and the locale ends in_review, deactivated, approver cleared. Importing into a draft or in_review locale needs no acknowledgement and does not change state. update_string and the Accept action never change lifecycle_state. Tests pin each case.
close_reason: Landed in 6d94656. A bulk re-import into an approved locale demotes it to in_review, clears the approver and deactivates it; the import still proceeds. Refused before any write unless acknowledged, on all three surfaces: --acknowledge-demotion on the CLI, a form field on both import routes, a panel confirmation. update_string and the per-string Accept are untouched. Review caught the panel appending the acknowledgement unconditionally, which made the dialog decorative on a stale locale list; fixed so a cache miss sends nothing and the route refuses and explains.

title: Seed DigitVA-authored layer translations on a fresh install, not only via migration
description:
Migration b6d2f4a9c1e7 seeds 214 DigitVA-authored translation strings, but it inserts only where a mas_instrument_locales row already exists. On a fresh install no locale rows exist at migration time -- the operator creates them later by importing workbooks -- so a new deployment receives 0 of the 214 strings and alembic will never run the migration again.

Verified 2026-09-20 on an empty database: 0 rows inserted. Nothing else covers it: no migration or seed command creates locale rows (app/commands/seed.py does not touch locales or translations; the only MasInstrumentLocales constructor in app/ is _get_or_create_locale). And no import can supply these strings, because no source workbook contains them -- that is why the migration exists.

Consequence: a new deployment's locales sit permanently at 0/2 on digitva_core and abha with the shared 'Medical and death documents' heading missing, and the only cure is hand-editing 214 strings in the admin panel.
design:
DECIDED by the owner 2026-09-20: keep this in a migration rather than a CLI seeder, and make the migration work on a fresh install.

Reading of the instruction, stated so it can be corrected: b6d2f4a9c1e7 no-ops on a fresh database because it only inserts where a mas_instrument_locales row already exists, and on a new install locales are created later by an operator import. So a new migration must create the twelve locale rows when they are absent -- lifecycle_state 'draft', is_active false, so nothing unreviewed is served and nothing is offered until an administrator acts -- and then insert the machine strings. A later operator import finds the existing row via _get_or_create_locale and fills in source_document/source_sha256, so the workbook import still works normally on top.

Because the machine drafts are not final, revising them ships as another migration that updates only source='machine' rows, never 'imported' and never 'edited'. That precedence is already documented in docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md.

Rows are inserted as source='machine' (not 'imported' as b6d2f4a9c1e7 originally did), so they are withheld from serving from the very first install rather than needing c1a4b6e8d3f2's relabel.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh database at head, with no workbook ever imported, holds the twelve locales as draft and inactive with their machine strings present and not served. Running the migration where locales already exist adds no duplicate locale rows and no duplicate strings. An administrator's edited row is never overwritten. A subsequent workbook import for one of those locales behaves exactly as it does today.
close_reason: Landed in 6d94656 as migration 7134cb5dc7b6, per the owner's decision to keep this in a migration rather than a CLI seeder. Creates the twelve locale rows when absent (draft, inactive) then inserts the 214 strings as source='machine', so a fresh install with no workbook ever imported ends with the drafts present and not served. Strings moved to resource/digitva_layer_translations_2026_09_20.csv instead of a third inlined copy, with a test parsing both applied migrations' literals to catch drift. Downgrade removes only untouched machine rows, never the locale rows.

title: Per-locale translation lifecycle: draft, in_review, approved
description:
A locale is served to interviewers once is_active is set, and nothing records that anyone reviewed it. Decided 2026-09-20 by the owner: incomplete, in-process or unverified translations must not be offered to users, and the decision should be recorded rather than held in an administrator's head.

Add lifecycle_state (draft | in_review | approved), approved_by_user_id (FK va_users.user_id, nullable) and approved_at (tz-aware, nullable) to mas_instrument_locales. title: Server accepts the client's own valid boolean as the questionnaire validity gate
description: app/services/web_intake_service.py:796-797 is the entire server-side form-validity check: 'if completion.get("valid") is not True: raise WebIntakeError(...)'. description: Constraint from owner: everything runs locally or in the browser, no external API. Query embedding either server-side ONNX or in-browser (transformers.js/WASM, model served from own origin). Blend with exact code/prefix match. notes:
Design + quality check 2026-09-25 (docs/planning/icd-semantic-search.md). Ladder measured on 30 grounded phrases: today's substring search 0/30 and 0/27 on narrative queries; dense over 31k titles caps ~50% hit@10 and bigger models do not help (bge-base flat-to-worse); RRF fusion hurts. BREAKTHROUGH: ranking the 63 VA causes (title+WHO definition embeddings) triples quality — top-3 20-21/30 and 18-19/27, MRR 0.57-0.61 — with MiniLM-L6 (23MB) and ~0.1MB vectors, far under the owner's 2GB browser ceiling. Definitions carry most of the gain. Next: phase-0 telemetry on the existing coding search first; then prototype the two-stage causes shape (rank causes client-side, pick code within cause via existing lexical search). Coverage table must come from annex+footnotes (VAs-12.01 icd10 cell is empty, footnote f holds the ranges; icd11 preterm codes uncovered). Optional levers: fine-tune on phrase->cause pairs, cross-encoder re-rank.
Layman-synonym check (owner's motivating case): heart attack, brain attack, brain stroke, paralysis (incl. paralysis attack, one-sided weakness) all hit their cause top-1 natively with bge-small; true idioms (fits — fixable by a synonym entry, falling sickness, dog bite madness, water in the lungs) still miss. Agreed mechanism: bounded synonym vocabulary, one curated reviewable list of local idioms per cause (mini-documents), maintained in the VA-definitions admin panel; phase-0 telemetry names which idioms actually occur.
Scope reframed by the owner 2026-09-25, two surfaces: (1) COD search box = clinicians typing diagnoses -> server-side doctor-shorthand expansion table (MI, CVA, CCF, Kochs, cor pulmonale, head injury...) + existing lexical endpoints, no model, no client cost; measured 33-query doctor batch: full names/synonyms work broadly top-1/2, only shorthand fails. (2) Narrative side = layperson language (water in the lungs, baby did not cry) -> the 63-cause semantic ranker (Phase B), natural input is the VA open narrative suggesting causes to the reviewer (CCVA-assist direction); typos survive semantically, idioms need the bounded vocabulary. Each surface gets its own telemetry.

title: Eleven of fourteen CHECK constraints have doubled, sometimes truncated names
description:
Measured on the dev database 2026-09-20. The metadata naming convention is ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s (app/__init__.py:42), and most models and migrations pass a name that already carries the ck_<table>_ prefix, so it is applied twice. Postgres then truncates at 63 characters, adding a hash suffix.

Doubled (11): map_project_site_odk (truncated, _9c4d), mas_org_level, va_forms, va_project_master x2 (one truncated, _108a), va_submissions x3, va_user_access_grants x3.
Clean (3): mas_instrument_locales_active_requires_approved (fixed 2026-09-20 by migration d2b5c7f9e4a3), va_smartva_form_runs_outcome, va_submission_payload_versions_status.

Note va_submission_payload_versions is clean even though its model passes the full prefixed name (app/models/va_submission_payload_versions.py:28), so whether the convention doubles depends on HOW the migration created the constraint -- a literal name in op.create_table renders as given, while op.create_check_constraint runs it through the convention. Establish which pattern each of the eleven used before changing any of them.
design:
Low priority because create and drop are self-consistent today: a migration that drops by the same over-long name it created renders the same doubled string. The real costs are that no name in the database matches what the model, the migration or the docs declare, so a DBA or a future migration searching for the declared name finds nothing; and a truncated name carries a hash that will change if the name is ever edited, so a drop by literal string is fragile.

The drift test (tests/migrations/test_schema_drift.py) cannot catch any of this: alembic's autogenerate does not compare CHECK constraint names. That is why it has been invisible.

Fix as one migration renaming all eleven, plus the model declarations passing only the discriminator. Verify every result against pg_constraint rather than assuming, the way d2b5c7f9e4a3 did. Consider whether a test asserting every ck_ name in a migrated database equals what the models declare would be worth adding -- that is the guard the drift test does not provide, and without it this recurs the next time someone adds a constraint.
acceptance_criteria: Every CHECK constraint in a migrated database carries the name its model declares. No name exceeds 63 characters. Each constraint still enforces what it did before the rename, pinned by a test per constraint or by one test that reproduces a violation for each. Migration upgrade/downgrade round-trips.
notes:
ANALYSIS 2026-09-20 before dispatching, because it changes what the guard must assert:

The models declare already-prefixed names (e.g. app/models/mas_organization.py name='ck_mas_org_level_depth_positive'), and the ck convention adds ck_<table>_ on top. So the DOUBLED name in the database is what the model renders -- a test comparing model-rendered names against pg_constraint would pass on all eleven and prove nothing. It would in fact fail on va_submission_payload_versions, whose database name is clean while its model would render the doubled form.

That asymmetry is because the database name depends on how the migration created the constraint: a literal name inside op.create_table lands as written, while op.create_check_constraint renders through the convention. So the database is not uniformly wrong; the model declarations are.

The guard therefore asserts shape, not just agreement: no CHECK constraint name may contain 'ck_<table>_ck_', and none may be 63 characters (Postgres's truncation point, which is how four of them acquired hash suffixes). Plus model-to-database agreement once the declarations are corrected.

Fourteen declarations across nine model files; three are already correct (mas_instrument_locales fixed by d2b5c7f9e4a3, va_smartva_form_runs, va_submission_payload_versions).
close_reason: Landed in b3e55cd. Thirteen of fourteen CHECK constraints renamed to what their models declare (migration fd232fab5987), model declarations now pass only the discriminator, and test_schema_drift.py gained the guard alembic cannot provide: no doubled ck_<table>_ck_<table>_ prefix, no 63-character truncated name, and two-way agreement between the migrated database and db.metadata. Shape assertions are the load-bearing ones -- a model-versus-database comparison alone would have passed on all thirteen. Count was eleven on dev and thirteen on a fresh chain replay, because alembic applies the convention through op.create_table regardless of a literal name, so dev's two clean ones were an accident of its history. Enforcement verified unchanged via pg_get_constraintdef, and the guard demonstrated failing when a doubled declaration is reintroduced.

title: CHECK constraint name is doubled and truncated in the database
description:

The metadata naming convention is ck_%(table_name)s_%(constraint_name)s, and both the model (app/models/mas_instrument_locales.py:67) and migration a3f7c1d9e6b4 pass the already-prefixed full name as constraint_name, so the prefix is applied twice and Postgres truncates at 63 characters.

title: Vendored vitest suite is timing-flaky under machine load
description:
On 2026-09-20, with the machine under sustained load (load average 4.27; the Claude desktop app alone at 77% CPU, Docker VM at 16.5% memory), the vendored package suite at vendor/who-va-2022 failed roughly two runs in three, with a DIFFERENT test failing each time:
- tests/web-audio-control.test.tsx > 'changes from start to stop and returns the saved recording' (vi.waitFor timeout, onAnswer never called)
- tests/web-validation-navigation.test.tsx:279 > 'scrolls to and focuses the first invalid question after Next' (expected vi.fn() called once, got 0)
- tests/web-component.tracer.test.ts > 'does not enable plaintext browser persistence by default' (expected undefined to be 'true')

The same suite passes 715/715 cleanly when the machine is quiet, including twice earlier the same day and once during this very investigation (run 1 of 3). A different test failing each run is the signature of timing flakiness, not a regression: a real defect would fail the same test deterministically. Vitest's own phase timings were several times their normal values during the failing runs (transform 30.7s, import 60.7s, environment 29.2s against ~3-15s normally).

Worth fixing because the suite is a release gate: if it fails two runs in three on a loaded developer machine, people will learn to re-run until green, which is exactly how a real failure gets waved through. The three tests named above all depend on async settling -- vi.waitFor, a focus/scroll side effect, and a tracer flag -- so the likely fix is explicit waits or fake timers rather than longer timeouts. Note the tracer one asserts a security-relevant default (plaintext browser persistence off), so it is the least acceptable of the three to leave flaky.

Observed while verifying digitva-thr.3/thr.4; not caused by them (the change in flight when it appeared was Python-only).

title: ODK site-mapping POST may not be idempotent under extreme latency
description:
Observed once on 2026-09-20 during a full-suite run under heavy concurrent machine load: tests/test_admin_api.py::AdminApiTests::test_odk_site_mappings failed with "'False' != 'True'". The test POSTs a mapping for (site_a, test_form) with form_smartvahiv='True', asserts the 201 response carries 'True' (that assertion PASSED), then GETs the mapping list and finds form_smartvahiv='False' for the same odk_form_id. The app's own slow_request log recorded duration_ms=151997.7 for the POST and 152010.1 for the GET -- roughly 152 seconds each. Suite wall time was 336s versus 115s on three earlier runs the same day.

Did NOT reproduce under normal load: the test alone passed 3/3, the whole file passed 45/45 three times, and the file combined with tests/services/test_instrument_translation_import.py passed 83/83, with no slow_request lines in any of the 7 runs. So this is not a regression from the digitva-thr.3/thr.4 work (which touched only the translation service and the vendored instrument) and the test is not deterministically broken.

Worth a look anyway because the failure shape is a read-after-write inconsistency, not a timeout: the write reported the right value and the immediately following read reported a different one. One hypothesis worth testing is that a POST retried under extreme latency creates a SECOND map_project_site_odk row for the same (site, odk_form_id) carrying column defaults, which the list endpoint's lookup then returns instead of the intended row -- i.e. the endpoint may not be idempotent and there may be no uniqueness constraint preventing a duplicate mapping. Check whether map_project_site_odk has a unique constraint on (site_id, odk_form_id) and whether the POST handler upserts or blindly inserts. If it blindly inserts, the same duplicate could be created by a double-click in the admin panel, not only by a pathological test run.
notes:
Second occurrence 2026-09-20, in a full-suite run on the translation-lifecycle tree. Same assertion: POST returns form_smartvahiv True, the following GET reads False.

This occurrence weakens the load hypothesis from the first one. The first failure came in a pathological run -- 336s wall time, individual requests logged at ~152s. This one came in a 146.9s full run, which is normal for this suite, with no slow_request lines. Isolated: tests/test_admin_api.py passed 45/45 three consecutive times immediately afterwards, and the test passed in two other full runs on the same tree.

So the sharper hypothesis is order-dependence or shared state inside the full suite rather than timeout pressure: something earlier in the full run leaves state that makes this read return the pre-write value. Worth running the full suite with -p no:randomly (if used) or bisecting the preceding test files rather than chasing timing. The changed code on this tree is the instrument-translation subsystem and app/schema_filters.py -- nothing touching map_project_site_odk -- so it is not a regression from that work.

title: geography extension flag is derived and served but has no consumer
description: _enabled_extensions() in app/routes/api/organization.py:591-597 derives 'geography' from count(MasOrgLevel) for the project and ships it in every form-options payload, but no code anywhere reads it: grepped every .py, .html, .js and .ts for enabled_extensions.includes('geography') / the literal string outside definitions, tests and docstrings, and there are zero consumers. The data ND01 collects as geography questions is server-injected instead (app/services/web_intake_service.py:721-723) per decision O4. Decide: either wire the intended consumer (if one was meant -- e.g. gating an org-unit picker or a geography display) or document the flag as informational-only so the 'gates content' claim in policy stops applying to it. The eight extension names are settled by the owner and geography stays one of them either way; this is about the flag's claimed effect, not its existence. Found 2026-09-19 while auditing layer-to-question contribution.
notes:
ARGUING AGAINST DELETION 2026-09-20, for the owner to accept or overrule.

The finding is accurate: nothing branches on the geography flag. No Python, template or TypeScript reads it, and the data it nominally covers (survey_state, survey_district, survey_block, site_individual_id) is server-injected after validation per decision O4 rather than gated by it.

But 'no consumer' is not the same as 'dead'. The flag is one of the eight names in ALL_DIGITVA_EXTENSIONS, which is a documented contract: a project declares which layers it collects. geography declares that this project collects geographic context -- which is true, and which the server then injects. A declaration that nothing branches on is still a record of intent, and enabled_extensions is read by clients outside this repository.

So deleting it would change a published contract to remove a true statement, for no behavioural gain. The cheaper and more honest fix is the one just applied: the extension table in docs/policy/va-form-project-configuration.md now says plainly that geography and intake_screen contribute NO instrument questions, cites O4, and notes that the flag is derived and served with no consumer. That removes the actual risk, which was never the flag itself -- it was the table inviting someone to author server-injected fields as interviewer questions.

Recommend closing as works-as-intended-now-documented. If the owner would rather remove it, that is a contract change and should go through the same care as adding one: check for external readers of enabled_extensions first.
close_reason: Closed as works-as-intended, now documented. The finding was accurate -- nothing branches on the geography flag -- but 'no consumer' is not 'dead': it is one of the eight names in ALL_DIGITVA_EXTENSIONS, a published contract by which a project declares which layers it collects, and that project does collect geographic context (server-injected per decision O4). Deleting it would change a public contract to remove a true statement for no behavioural gain. The real risk was the policy table inviting someone to author those server-injected fields as interviewer questions; that table now says 'No instrument questions' and cites O4 (8cdb1fd). If the owner still wants it removed, treat it as a contract change and check for external readers of enabled_extensions first.

MEASURED 2026-09-20, and the picture is narrower than the description implies.

Dev holds 2,414 WHO_2022_VA mappings, the frozen workbook 2,380, and every workbook code is present on dev -- nothing has been lost. The delta is exactly 34 rows whose source_sheet is 'admin_cod_bucket_editor' rather than 'ICD_Mapped', so they were added deliberately through the admin editor, and they are precisely identifiable by that marker:

G46, G47, I11, I46, I50, K64, K70, K72, K73, K75, K76, R03 and 22 more.

Those are clinically plausible gaps in the WHO derivation -- heart failure (I50), hypertensive heart disease (I11), cardiac arrest (I46), the K70-K76 liver group, R03 abnormal blood-pressure reading. This reads as real curation, not accidental divergence, which argues for freezing rather than resetting.

CORRECTION to my own first diff: it appeared to show all 2,380 codes mapped to a different bucket. That was a representation artifact, not drift -- the workbook writes VAs-01.04 and the database stores vas_01_04 for the same node. There is no semantic bucket difference on the 2,380. Anyone re-running this comparison should normalise the node code before concluding anything.

Not yet verified: the description's 'label drift on 86 codes'. My comparison used node codes, not labels, so that claim is still open and should be checked separately before it is acted on or dismissed.

1,814 dev rows carry a mapping_note (e.g. A33 'Age/context sensitive: A33 is excluded from general tetanus'), so the curation on this scheme is substantial and a reset would discard more than the 34 rows.

title: ND01's duration constraint rejects values its own synced data contains
description:
Observation, not a defect to fix. Decided 2026-09-20 by the owner: keep sa13-sa19 exactly as deployed -- dataType 'string', ND01's verbatim constraint regex(.,'^(?!0{1,3}$)\\d{1,3}$'), integer-only, 1 to 3 digits, zero rejected. An earlier instruction to allow decimals was withdrawn in favour of fidelity to the deployed instrument.

What the investigation turned up, measured on the dev database: 1,592 submissions carry sa13, all as JSON strings, and the distinct values include '0', '01', '03' and '05'. The constraint's negative lookahead rejects '0', so real ODK-synced data contains a value the deployed form's own constraint refuses. Either those submissions predate the constraint, or the deployed ODK form does not enforce it.

Recorded so that a future reader does not treat this as a web-form bug, and so that anyone who later re-validates historical submissions knows to expect failures on legitimately synced rows. ODK is the source of truth for synced content; the web form matching it verbatim is correct even where the constraint and the data disagree.
design: No code change. If this is ever revisited, the question to answer first is whether a zero duration is meaningful in the field -- if it is, ND01's constraint is the thing that is wrong, and changing DigitVA's copy alone would put the two capture channels out of step. Any change belongs upstream in the ODK form, not here.
acceptance_criteria: No action required. Close if the owner confirms the observation is understood and no further work is wanted.
close_reason: Observation recorded and explained to the owner 2026-09-20; no action wanted. sa13-sa19 keep ND01's verbatim constraint by the owner's decision, and dev's synced data contains '0' for sa13, which that constraint's negative lookahead rejects. Either those submissions predate the constraint or the deployed ODK form never enforced it. Kept in the record for three reasons: nobody should mistake the web form rejecting 0 for a DigitVA bug, anyone re-validating historical submissions should expect failures on legitimately synced rows, and any fix belongs upstream in the ODK form since changing DigitVA's copy alone would put the two capture channels out of step.
